description: AgriMind RAG benchmark: questions written against the bundled demonstration knowledge base. 'relevant' lists the document(s) that contain the answer; 'reference' is a short gold answer taken from that document.

items.question: What are the symptoms of late blight in tomato?
items.reference: Large irregular water-soaked greasy grey-green patches on leaves that turn brown-black, with white downy growth on the leaf underside in humid weather and firm brown patches on fruit. It spreads fast in cool, humid, cloudy weather.

items.question: How is tomato yellow leaf curl virus spread and how can I manage it?
items.reference: It is transmitted by the whitefly Bemisia tabaci. Infected plants cannot be cured and should be uprooted early; raise seedlings under insect-proof net, use tolerant hybrids, yellow sticky traps, border crops like maize, and manage whiteflies with neem products or rotated insecticides.

items.question: What causes blossom-end rot in tomato fruits?
items.reference: Calcium deficiency in the fruit, made worse by irregular soil moisture; maintain uniform moisture and adequate calcium.

items.question: What spacing should be used when transplanting tomato seedlings?
items.reference: Transplant 25–30 day old seedlings; common spacing is 60 × 45 cm for determinate varieties and 90 × 60 cm or wider for staked indeterminate hybrids.

items.question: How do I control fruit borer in tomato?
items.reference: Use pheromone traps (5 per acre), African marigold trap crop, Trichogramma releases, HaNPV or Bt sprays, and insecticides only after the economic threshold.

items.question: How can I recognise common rust on maize leaves?
items.reference: Small oval to elongated cinnamon-brown powdery pustules on both leaf surfaces, darkening with age, favoured by 16–23 °C and high humidity.

items.question: What does northern corn leaf blight look like?
items.reference: Long cigar-shaped grey-green to tan lesions 2.5–15 cm long, starting on lower leaves, caused by Exserohilum turcicum.

items.question: How do I manage fall armyworm in maize?
items.reference: Synchronous early sowing, scouting whorls twice weekly, pheromone traps, sand and lime in the whorl, neem oil, and approved insecticides such as emamectin benzoate, spinetoram or chlorantraniliprole into the whorl when 10% of plants are damaged.

items.question: How should potato late blight be managed?
items.reference: Use certified seed tubers and resistant varieties, earth up rows, follow forecasts, protectant mancozeb sprays and systemic combinations like metalaxyl + mancozeb when blight appears, and destroy haulms 10–15 days before harvest.

items.question: How do I control bacterial spot on capsicum?
items.reference: Use certified treated seed and healthy transplants, avoid overhead irrigation, rotate 2–3 years away from pepper and tomato, use copper sprays and remove crop debris.

items.question: What is the low, medium and high rating for available nitrogen in soil?
items.reference: Available nitrogen below 280 kg/ha is low, 280–560 kg/ha is medium and above 560 kg/ha is high.

items.question: My soil pH is 8.8. What does that mean and what should I do?
items.reference: pH above 8.5 is strongly alkaline or sodic soil; it needs reclamation with gypsum according to the gypsum requirement, plus drainage.

items.question: How do I take a soil sample for testing?
items.reference: After harvest and before fertiliser, take 10–15 sub-samples in a zig-zag at 0–15 cm depth avoiding bunds and shade, mix, quarter down to about 500 g, shade-dry and label.

items.question: Which leaves turn yellow first in nitrogen deficiency?
items.reference: Nitrogen deficiency causes uniform pale yellowing starting on older, lower leaves, with stunted growth; sulphur deficiency shows on younger leaves.

items.question: How much nitrogen does urea contain and what is in DAP?
items.reference: Urea contains 46% N; DAP contains 18% N and 46% P2O5.

items.question: What is the crop coefficient of maize at mid-season?
items.reference: According to FAO-56 the mid-season Kc of grain maize is 1.20 (initial 0.30, late 0.35–0.60).

items.question: How much water can drip irrigation save?
items.reference: Drip saves 30–60% water compared with flood irrigation and has 85–95% application efficiency.

items.question: Which is the most critical stage to irrigate maize?
items.reference: Tasseling and silking is the most critical stage for maize, followed by grain filling.

items.question: What is alternate wetting and drying in paddy?
items.reference: Letting the field water fall to about 15 cm below the soil surface, checked with a field tube, before re-flooding, except at flowering; it saves 15–30% water.

items.question: What is the System of Rice Intensification?
items.reference: SRI uses 8–12 day old seedlings, one per hill at 25 × 25 cm, intermittent irrigation, cono-weeder weeding and more organic manure, needing only 5–7.5 kg seed per hectare.

items.question: What are the symptoms of rice blast?
items.reference: Spindle-shaped leaf spots with grey centres and brown margins; neck blast breaks the panicle and leaves grains empty; favoured by high nitrogen and humid weather.

items.question: When should I harvest paddy?
items.reference: When 80–85% of grains in the panicle turn straw-coloured; dry to 12–14% moisture before storage, after draining the field 10–15 days before harvest.

items.question: What is the recommended seed rate and spacing for ragi?
items.reference: 10 kg seed per hectare in lines 30 cm apart (22.5 cm for late sowing), plants 7.5–10 cm apart.

items.question: How do I prepare neem seed kernel extract?
items.reference: Soak 5 kg powdered neem seed kernel overnight in 10 litres of water, filter, dilute to 100 litres and add a little soap as a sticker.

items.question: What precautions should I take while spraying pesticides?
items.reference: Read the label, wear gloves, mask, full sleeves and boots, don't eat or smoke, spray in calm morning or evening not against wind, avoid flowering bees and water bodies, respect the waiting period and dispose containers safely.

items.question: How is vermicompost made?
items.reference: Eisenia fetida earthworms convert dung and crop residues into manure in 45–60 days under shade with 40–50% moisture.

items.question: Which crops are grown in the Rabi season?
items.reference: Rabi crops are sown October–November and harvested February–April: wheat, chickpea, rabi jowar, safflower, linseed, mustard, onion and vegetables.

items.question: What crops suit the northern dry zone of Karnataka?
items.reference: Black cotton soils with 500–700 mm rain: jowar, tur, Bengal gram, sunflower, cotton and bajra, with paddy in command areas.

items.question: What should I sow if the monsoon is delayed?
items.reference: Short-duration varieties and crops like green gram, horse gram, cowpea and fodder, or transplant ragi from a protectively irrigated nursery, following the district contingency plan.

items.question: How much money does PM-KISAN give farmers?
items.reference: ₹6,000 per year in three equal instalments of ₹2,000 through DBT to Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts; e-KYC is mandatory.

items.question: What premium does a farmer pay under PMFBY for a kharif crop?
items.reference: A maximum of 2% of the sum insured for Kharif food and oilseed crops (1.5% Rabi, 5% commercial/horticultural).

items.question: What subsidy is available for drip irrigation for a small farmer?
items.reference: Under PMKSY Per Drop More Crop small and marginal farmers get 55% assistance (45% for others) for up to 5 hectares.

items.question: What is the interest rate on a Kisan Credit Card crop loan?
items.reference: 7% per year under the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme, with a 3% prompt repayment incentive giving an effective 4%.

items.question: Who can join the PM Kisan Maan-Dhan pension scheme?
items.reference: Small and marginal farmers owning up to 2 hectares aged 18–40, contributing ₹55–200 per month, for a ₹3,000 monthly pension after 60.

items.question: ಟೊಮೆಟೊದಲ್ಲಿ ಎಲೆ ಮುರುಟು ವೈರಸ್ ಹೇಗೆ ಹರಡುತ್ತದೆ?
items.reference: Tomato yellow leaf curl virus is spread by the whitefly Bemisia tabaci.

items.question: धान की फसल में ब्लास्ट रोग के लक्षण क्या हैं?
items.reference: Spindle-shaped leaf spots with grey centres and brown margins; neck blast leaves grains empty.
